extraction_metadata.notes: Reverse-engineered from arXiv:2610.22709 (Oct 2026). AI/ML image reconstruction for coded-aperture instruments with embedded real-time path.

title: A New AI/ML Based Image Reconstruction Technique for Coded-Aperture Instruments
subtitle_or_tagline: Embedded real-time reconstruction for coded-aperture imaging
topic: A new AI/ML-based image reconstruction method for coded-aperture instruments that provides a pathway for embedded real-time reconstruction. Coded-aperture imaging is used in high-energy astrophysics and security scanning where focusing optics are not feasible; the encoded mask pattern requires computational decoding. The proposed method replaces or augments traditional iterative decoders with a trained neural network capable of running on embedded hardware at acquisition rate.

components.name: Coded-mask encoder
components.role: Physical mask casts a shadow pattern on the detector; the shadow encodes the sky/image

components.name: Detector readout
components.role: Records the shadow pattern with noise and limited photon statistics

components.name: AI/ML reconstructor
components.role: Neural network decodes the shadow pattern into a reconstructed image

components.name: Embedded runtime
components.role: Runs the reconstructor on-device for real-time feedback

architecture.data_flow: Source sky + coded mask -> shadowgram on detector -> AI/ML reconstructor -> reconstructed image (real-time)

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Acquire shadowgram from coded-aperture detector.
Step 3 - Run neural-network reconstructor on embedded hardware.
Step 4 - Return reconstructed image at acquisition rate.
Step 5 - Optional iterative refinement if compute budget allows.
key_claims: Enables real-time reconstruction on embedded hardware (not just offline post-processing).
Pathway for deployment in resource-constrained instruments (small satellites, fielded detectors).
Replaces or augments traditional iterative decoders with a learned reconstruction.
Maintains reconstruction quality despite photon-limited, noisy shadowgrams.
caveats_or_warnings: Learned reconstructors can hallucinate sources not present in the data; uncertainty quantification is critical.
Generalization across mask patterns, detector responses, and source distributions requires careful training.
Real-time performance depends on hardware availability on the instrument.
